problem_statement_vague: The voice assistant's view of a lane's gate ignores the Director's feedback comments on the issue thread. When the Director sends a lane back for revision the desktop card shows REVISING, but raven has no record of the feedback, has no notion of that phase, and still announces the lane as ready to test.
problem_statement_precise: daemons/raven-core/raven_core/tools/lane_gate_tool.py mirrors shell/src/utils/laneGate.ts but is missing the third lane-channel prefix and the phase resolver. Expected, matching the TS side exactly: (1) a module constant for the prefix literal `DIRECTOR FEEDBACK` alongside `GATE_REPORT_PREFIX` and `PR_OPENED_PREFIX`; (2) `_fold_gate` returns a state with fields `report`, `report_at`, `pr`, `feedback`, `feedback_at` (inert value `{"report": None, "report_at": None, "pr": False, "feedback": None, "feedback_at": None}`, also returned when spawned_at is None or comments is not a list), where DIRECTOR FEEDBACK comments are subject to the same strictly-newer-than-spawn guard as reports (a feedback comment older than the spawn leaves the state inert) and latest-wins (two feedback comments after the spawn → `feedback` is the later body); (3) a phase function mirroring `gatePhase()` that takes a fold state or None and returns one of the strings `working`, `at-gate`, `revising`, `pr-opened` by pure precedence: None → `working`; `pr` true → `pr-opened`; no report → `working` (so feedback with no report is still `working`); feedback_at strictly newer than report_at → `revising`; otherwise `at-gate`. Reproduce with spawn `2026-06-11T10:00:00.000Z` and comments report@11:00, feedback@12:00, re-gate report@13:00, PR OPENED@14:00: the expected phases for the prefixes [], [report], [report, feedback], [report, feedback, regate], [all four], [feedback only] are working, at-gate, revising, at-gate, pr-opened, working respectively. Today `_fold_gate` ignores DIRECTOR FEEDBACK entirely and no phase resolver exists. In addition, `_whats_ready_to_test()` in the same module must stop announcing a lane whose latest GATE REPORT has strictly newer DIRECTOR FEEDBACK: such a lane is not ready; with one live lane (issue 372, spawned 2026-06-11T00:00Z) whose issue comments are `GATE REPORT — pass 1` at 01:00 and `DIRECTOR FEEDBACK — the fold misses the third prefix` at 02:00, the result must have `count` 0, `lanes` `[]`, and `spoken` exactly `"Nothing's at the gate yet, sir — 1 lane still working."` (the existing working-lane line). Once a newer GATE REPORT is appended (03:00), the lane is ready again: `count` 1 and `lanes` `[{"issue": 372, "title": "fix(raven): gate fold parity"}]`. PR OPENED continues to outrank everything. The mesh hop is `mesh_invoke` returning `{ok, number, title, comments}`; the ledger is `$AETHER_DATA_DIR/spawns/requests.jsonl`.

problem_statement_vague: Two of the app ids the voice assistant is told it can open don't exist any more, so when the model dutifully uses them the open fails. The suggested editor app ids are stale relative to what the desktop shell actually registers.
problem_statement_precise: `APP_HINTS` in daemons/raven-core/raven_core/tools/viewer_tool.py (the id hints seeded into the `open_app` tool declaration) contains `markdown-editor` and `text-editor`, but the shell's app registry (shell/src/apps/*/index.ts, the `id:` field of each app's index) registers those apps under different ids — the apps named 'Markdown Editor' and 'Text Editor' do not have ids `markdown-editor` / `text-editor`. Every entry in APP_HINTS must be a verbatim id present in the shell registry; today two entries are not, so the model is taught ids that always fail. Reproduce: collect the `id:` values from shell/src/apps/*/index.ts and diff against `viewer_tool.APP_HINTS` — the set difference must be empty.

+"""App-id resolution semantics for the viewer tool (#243): name-aware
+fuzzy matching ('text editor' must find id 'text-viewer'), the `id`
+alias for open_app's app_id argument, failure results that always carry
+the valid ids, and an anti-drift gate pinning APP_HINTS to the shell's
+live app registry source.
+
+The mesh hop is mocked (patch viewer_tool.mesh_invoke), so these run
+without a live mesh.
+"""
+import asyncio
+import re
+import sys
+import unittest.mock as mock
+from pathlib import Path
+
+sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent.parent))
+
+# Same global mock test_tool_registry.py uses: importing raven_core.tools
+# (the package __init__) pulls session_context's deep import chain.
+if "raven_core.session_context" not in sys.modules:
+    sys.modules["raven_core.session_context"] = mock.MagicMock()
+
+import pytest
+
+import raven_core.tools.viewer_tool as vt
+
+REGISTRY = [
+    {"id": "browser", "name": "Browser"},
+    {"id": "kanban-board", "name": "Kanban"},
+    {"id": "markdown-viewer", "name": "Markdown Editor"},
+    {"id": "text-viewer", "name": "Text Editor"},
+    {"id": "terminal", "name": "Terminal"},
+]
+REGISTRY_IDS = [a["id"] for a in REGISTRY]
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------- fuzzy match
+
+def test_fuzzy_matches_display_name_when_id_drifted():
+    # The drift that kept #243 alive: apps NAMED 'Markdown Editor' /
+    # 'Text Editor' register under -viewer ids.
+    assert vt._fuzzy_match_app("text-editor", REGISTRY) == ["text-viewer"]
+    assert vt._fuzzy_match_app("markdown editor", REGISTRY) == ["markdown-viewer"]
+
+
+def test_fuzzy_exact_id_still_wins():
+    assert vt._fuzzy_match_app("kanban-board", REGISTRY) == ["kanban-board"]
+
+
+def test_fuzzy_substring_containment_on_ids():
+    assert vt._fuzzy_match_app("kanban", REGISTRY) == ["kanban-board"]
+
+
+def test_fuzzy_no_match_returns_empty():
+    assert vt._fuzzy_match_app("flux-capacitor", REGISTRY) == []
+    assert vt._fuzzy_match_app("", REGISTRY) == []
+
+
+def test_fuzzy_tolerates_nameless_entries():
+    # The fallback path wraps bare ids as {'id': ...} dicts with no name.
+    assert vt._fuzzy_match_app("text viewer", [{"id": "text-viewer"}]) == [
+        "text-viewer"
+    ]
+
+
+# ------------------------------------------------------------------ open_app
+
+def _mesh(responses):
+    """Mock mesh_invoke returning queued responses per surface."""
+
+    async def invoke(surface, payload):
+        handler = responses[surface]
+        return handler.pop(0) if isinstance(handler, list) else handler
+
+    return invoke
+
+
+def test_open_app_resolves_name_and_retries_once():
+    miss = {"ok": False, "available": REGISTRY_IDS}
+    hit = {"ok": True, "windowId": "w1"}
+    responses = {
+        "viewer_desktop.open_app": [miss, hit],
+        "viewer_desktop.list_apps": {"apps": REGISTRY},
+    }
+    with mock.patch.object(vt, "mesh_invoke", _mesh(responses)):
+        result = asyncio.run(vt._open_app("text editor", ""))
+    assert result == {
+        "ok": True,
+        "app_id": "text-viewer",
+        "resolved_from": "text editor",
+        "window_id": "w1",
+    }
+
+
+def test_open_app_unknown_id_returns_available_apps():
+    miss = {"ok": False, "available": REGISTRY_IDS}
+    responses = {
+        "viewer_desktop.open_app": [miss],
+        "viewer_desktop.list_apps": {"apps": REGISTRY},
+    }
+    with mock.patch.object(vt, "mesh_invoke", _mesh(responses)):
+        result = asyncio.run(vt._open_app("flux-capacitor", ""))
+    assert result["ok"] is False
+    assert result["error"] == "unknown_app"
+    assert result["available_apps"] == REGISTRY_IDS
+    assert result["did_you_mean"] is None
+
+
+def test_open_app_falls_back_to_bare_ids_when_registry_read_fails():
+    queue = [
+        {"ok": False, "available": REGISTRY_IDS},
+        {"ok": True, "windowId": "w2"},
+    ]
+
+    async def invoke(surface, payload):

+
+    with mock.patch.object(vt, "mesh_invoke", invoke):
+        result = asyncio.run(vt._open_app("kanban", ""))
+    assert result["ok"] is True
+    assert result["app_id"] == "kanban-board"

+
+def test_open_app_empty_id_still_lists_apps():

+"""App-id resolution semantics for the viewer tool (#243): name-aware
+fuzzy matching ('text editor' must find id 'text-viewer'), the `id`
+alias for open_app's app_id argument, failure results that always carry
+the valid ids, and an anti-drift gate pinning APP_HINTS to the shell's
+live app registry source.
+
+The mesh hop is mocked (patch viewer_tool.mesh_invoke), so these run
+without a live mesh.
+"""
+import asyncio
+import re
+import sys
+import unittest.mock as mock
+from pathlib import Path
+
+sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent.parent))
+
+# Same global mock test_tool_registry.py uses: importing raven_core.tools
+# (the package __init__) pulls session_context's deep import chain.
+if "raven_core.session_context" not in sys.modules:
+    sys.modules["raven_core.session_context"] = mock.MagicMock()
+
+import pytest
+
+import raven_core.tools.viewer_tool as vt
+
+REGISTRY = [
+    {"id": "browser", "name": "Browser"},
+    {"id": "kanban-board", "name": "Kanban"},
+    {"id": "markdown-viewer", "name": "Markdown Editor"},
+    {"id": "text-viewer", "name": "Text Editor"},
+    {"id": "terminal", "name": "Terminal"},
+]
+REGISTRY_IDS = [a["id"] for a in REGISTRY]
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------- fuzzy match
+
+def test_fuzzy_matches_display_name_when_id_drifted():
+    # The drift that kept #243 alive: apps NAMED 'Markdown Editor' /
+    # 'Text Editor' register under -viewer ids.
+    assert vt._fuzzy_match_app("text-editor", REGISTRY) == ["text-viewer"]
+    assert vt._fuzzy_match_app("markdown editor", REGISTRY) == ["markdown-viewer"]
+
+
+def test_fuzzy_exact_id_still_wins():
+    assert vt._fuzzy_match_app("kanban-board", REGISTRY) == ["kanban-board"]
+
+
+def test_fuzzy_substring_containment_on_ids():
+    assert vt._fuzzy_match_app("kanban", REGISTRY) == ["kanban-board"]
+
+
+def test_fuzzy_no_match_returns_empty():
+    assert vt._fuzzy_match_app("flux-capacitor", REGISTRY) == []
+    assert vt._fuzzy_match_app("", REGISTRY) == []
+
+
+def test_fuzzy_tolerates_nameless_entries():
+    # The fallback path wraps bare ids as {'id': ...} dicts with no name.
+    assert vt._fuzzy_match_app("text viewer", [{"id": "text-viewer"}]) == [
+        "text-viewer"
+    ]

+def _mesh(responses):

+
+    async def invoke(surface, payload):
+        handler = responses[surface]
+        return handler.pop(0) if isinstance(handler, list) else handler

+        result = asyncio.run(vt._open_app("text editor", ""))

+        "ok": True,
+        "app_id": "text-viewer",
+        "resolved_from": "text editor",
+        "window_id": "w1",
+    }
+
+

+    miss = {"ok": False, "available": REGISTRY_IDS}

+        "viewer_desktop.list_apps": {"apps": REGISTRY},

+

+    queue = [
+        {"ok": False, "available": REGISTRY_IDS},
+        {"ok": True, "windowId": "w2"},
+    ]
+
+    async def invoke(surface, payload):
+        if surface == "viewer_desktop.list_apps":
+            raise vt.MeshUnavailable("down")
+        return queue.pop(0)
+
+    with mock.patch.object(vt, "mesh_invoke", invoke):
+        result = asyncio.run(vt._open_app("kanban", ""))
+    assert result["ok"] is True
+    assert result["app_id"] == "kanban-board"
+
+
+def test_open_app_empty_id_still_lists_apps():
+    responses = {"viewer_desktop.list_apps": {"apps": REGISTRY}}
+    with mock.patch.object(vt, "mesh_invoke", _mesh(responses)):
+        result = asyncio.run(vt._open_app("", ""))
+    assert result["ok"] is False
+    assert result["error"] == "bad_app_id"
+    assert result["available_apps"] == REGISTRY_IDS

+

+    # Older prompt examples taught open_app({ id: ... }); the handler
+    # must not dead-end on the alias.
+    hit = {"ok": True, "windowId": "w3"}
+    responses = {"viewer_desktop.open_app": [hit]}
+    with mock.patch.object(vt, "mesh_invoke", _mesh(responses)):
+        result = asyncio.run(vt.handle_call_async("open_app", {"id": "browser"}))
+    assert result == {"ok": True, "app_id": "browser", "window_id": "w3"}
+
+
+# ----------------------------------------------------------------- anti-drift
+
+def _shell_registry_ids():
+    """Extract registered app ids from the shell's auto-glob source."""
+    apps_dir = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] / "shell" / "src" / "apps"
+    if not apps_dir.is_dir():
+        pytest.skip("shell/src/apps not present in this checkout")
+    ids = set()
+    for index in apps_dir.glob("*/index.ts"):
+        m = re.search(r"id:\s*['\"]([^'\"]+)['\"]", index.read_text())
+        if m:
+            ids.add(m.group(1))
+    return ids
+
+
+def test_app_hints_exist_in_shell_registry():
+    # APP_HINTS is deliberately a non-load-bearing subset, but every
+    # entry must be a VERBATIM registry id — 'markdown-editor' /
+    # 'text-editor' drifted dead once (#243) and the model dutifully
+    # passed them.
+    registry = _shell_registry_ids()
+    stale = set(vt.APP_HINTS) - registry
+    assert not stale, f"APP_HINTS entries missing from shell registry: {stale}"

+issue that already holds a requested-or-live lane record (requested |
+spawned | teardown_failed — the capacity set) refuses at the source and
+points at the existing card/lane; batch calls arm the rest and name the
+skipped. Pinned against the #383 duplicate-request parity fixture
+(tests/lane_fixtures.py) in both duplicate directions: a live lane refuses
+a fresh arm even when its dead duplicate is newer, and dead records alone
+never block one.

+The github.get_issue hop is mocked (and its call list pinned — a skipped
+issue must cost zero API reads); everything else is real file I/O against
+AETHER_DATA_DIR, the lane_proceed-gate rig.
+"""
+import asyncio
+import json
+import sys
+import unittest.mock as mock
+from pathlib import Path
+

+    ledger = tmp_path / "spawns" / "requests.jsonl"
+    ledger.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    ledger.write_text("".join(json.dumps(rec) + "\n" for rec in lines), encoding="utf-8")
+    return ledger
+

problem_statement_precise: `_lane_status(issue)` in daemons/raven-core/raven_core/tools/close_lane_tool.py resolves an issue's lane state by taking the NEWEST lane record for that issue and returning its status. When an issue has an older record that is live (`spawned`, or `teardown_failed`) and a newer duplicate record that died (`failed` then `dismissed`) — the ledger shape in tests/lane_fixtures.py `DUPLICATE_LANE_LINES` for issue 374 — it returns `dismissed`, and `_close_lane(374, confirmed=False)` refuses with `lane #374 is dismissed, not closeable` instead of returning the pending confirmation ask. When no record is closeable, the newest record's status is still returned so the existing spoken refusals (`closed`, `requested`, other) keep working. Relay and teardown lines remain ignored.

meta.commit_subject: fix(spawn): lane fold liveness parity — the newest LIVE record wins per issue (#397)

problem_statement_vague: "What's ready to test" reports one live lane when the desktop shows two. A lane whose issue got a second, failed-and-dismissed spawn request disappears from raven's list of live lanes even though the first lane is still running.
problem_statement_precise: `_live_lanes()` in daemons/raven-core/raven_core/tools/lane_gate_tool.py folds `$AETHER_DATA_DIR/spawns/requests.jsonl` per issue and treats the issue as live only if its NEWEST lane record has status `spawned`. With the July-14 duplicate-request shape (tests/lane_fixtures.py `DUPLICATE_LANE_LINES`: issue 371 spawned once; issue 374 with an older record `arm-374-a` that reached `spawned` at 2026-07-14T23:49:19+00:00 and a newer record `arm-374-b` that went `failed` then `dismissed`; interleaved relay, gate, teardown and telemetry lines), it returns only issue 371. Expected: per issue, the newest record whose status is `spawned` wins, so the result lists issues `[371, 374]` (sorted), and 374's `title` (`chore(docs): §10 gotchas`) and `spawned_at` (the parsed `2026-07-14T23:49:19+00:00`) come from the live record, never the dead duplicate. An issue with no spawned record (e.g. after `arm-374-a` is later `closed`) still folds out. Relay/teardown lines stay excluded by kind.

                 spawned_ts_by_id[rec_id] = obj["ts"]
     lanes: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
     for issue, ids in sorted(lane_ids_by_issue.items()):
-        newest = ids[-1]
-        if status_by_id.get(newest) != "spawned":
+        # The newest LIVE record wins (#383): a dead newer duplicate — the
+        # July-14 374 shape, a second arm that failed preflight and was
+        # dismissed — must never mask the live lane beside it. Only an issue
+        # with NO spawned record folds out.
+        live = next((i for i in reversed(ids) if status_by_id.get(i) == "spawned"), None)
+        if live is None:
             continue

             {

+                "title": title_by_id.get(live, ""),
+                "spawned_at": _parse_ts(spawned_ts_by_id.get(live)),

meta.commit_subject: fix(spawn): lane fold liveness parity — the newest LIVE record wins per issue (#397)

problem_statement_vague: Voice 'proceed on lane 374' and 'revise lane 374' are refused as 'not live' after a duplicate spawn request on 374 failed and was dismissed, even though the original lane 374 is still running.
problem_statement_precise: `_lane_status(issue)` in daemons/raven-core/raven_core/tools/lane_proceed_tool.py (also used by lane_revise_tool) returns the status of the NEWEST lane record for the issue. For the ledger in tests/lane_fixtures.py `DUPLICATE_LANE_LINES`, issue 374 has an older record that is `spawned` and a newer duplicate that is `failed` then `dismissed`, so `_lane_status(374)` returns `dismissed` and both `_lane_proceed(374, confirmed=False)` and `lane_revise_tool._lane_revise(374, confirmed=False)` refuse with a 'not live' error instead of returning the pending confirmation ask. Expected: status first, newest among the live — if any lane record for the issue is `spawned`, `_lane_status` returns `spawned`, and both tools return a result with `pending` True on the first (unconfirmed) call. When no record is live, the newest record's status is returned as before (after `arm-374-a` closes, `_lane_status(374)` is `dismissed` and proceed refuses with an error containing `not live`). The old guarantee that a newer live arm wins over an older dismissed one must still hold.
patch:
diff --git a/daemons/raven-core/raven_core/tools/lane_proceed_tool.py b/daemons/raven-core/raven_core/tools/lane_proceed_tool.py
index 03bcc36..02b50bb 100644
--- a/daemons/raven-core/raven_core/tools/lane_proceed_tool.py
+++ b/daemons/raven-core/raven_core/tools/lane_proceed_tool.py
@@ -103,8 +104,15 @@ def _lane_status(issue: int) -> str | None:
             status_by_id[rec_id] = status
     if not lane_ids:
         return None
-    # Newest arm wins: an old dismissed request for the same issue must not
-    # shadow the live lane that replaced it.
+    # The executor's resolution rule, mirrored (spawnService.liveLane — status
+    # FIRST, newest among the matches): the newest LIVE record wins, so
+    # neither duplicate direction shadows the other — an old dismissed arm
+    # never hides its live replacement, and a dead newer duplicate never
+    # hides the live lane beside it (#383, the July-14 374 shape). With no
+    # live record, the newest record's status shapes the spoken refusal.
+    for rec_id in reversed(lane_ids):
+        if status_by_id.get(rec_id) == "spawned":
+            return "spawned"
     return status_by_id.get(lane_ids[-1])

problem_statement_vague: The HTTP load generator reports streaming requests as successful even when the server emitted an error event mid-stream or the connection dropped before the response finished. Those requests should show up as failures, with a reason, not as completed requests.
problem_statement_precise: In the benchmark harness's HTTP client (pagedserve/bench/load.py, `_one_request`, reached through `run_http_benchmark`), a streaming request against /v1/chat/completions or /v1/completions is recorded as a success as soon as at least one token chunk arrived, regardless of how the stream ended. Two cases are wrong. (1) If the server returns HTTP 200 and then sends an SSE event whose JSON has a top-level `error` object (e.g. `{"error": {"message": "engine died", "type": "server_error"}}`) after some tokens, the event is silently skipped because it carries no `choices`, and the request ends up `success=True`. Expected: `success=False` with `error` containing the server's message text ("engine died" in that example), and the failed record should carry the wall-clock time (perf_counter seconds) at which the request gave up in a field named `end_s`, so the run's duration can include failed requests; today a failed record has no such timestamp. (2) If the stream ends (the body closes) after token chunks but without a `[DONE]` sentinel and without any choice carrying a non-null `finish_reason`, the request is still a success. Expected: `success=False` with an `error` string that says the stream ended before completion (containing the words "before completion"). A stream that ends with `[DONE]` or with a chunk whose choice has a `finish_reason` remains a success. Reproduce with an httpx.MockTransport that streams `data: <json>\n\n` lines and pass it as `transport=` to `run_http_benchmark`.

+"""The golden gate's tie-break rule (scripts/check_golden.py): a mismatch is excused only
+when the two disputed tokens are both at the top within the measured noise. It used to
+look at the top-2 gap alone, which also excused an unrelated wrong token whenever the top
+two happened to be close."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import torch
+
+from pagedserve.sched.request import SamplingParams
+from tests.test_engine import make_engine, prompts
+
+sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "scripts"))
+from check_golden import tie_gap  # noqa: E402

+def test_tie_gap_is_about_the_disputed_pair() -> None:
+    eng = make_engine()
+    ids = prompts(1)[0]
+    req = eng.add_request("probe", ids, SamplingParams.greedy(1))
+    so = eng.scheduler.schedule()
+    with torch.inference_mode():
+        logits = eng.step_logits(so)[0].float()
+    eng.abort_request(req.request_id)
+    eng.backend.free_sequence(req.seq_id)

meta.commit_subject: Fix the golden gate, the Serverless worker and the benchmark harness (review findings)

problem_statement_vague: Benchmark summaries overstate throughput when some requests fail: a run where failed requests kept timing out after the last successful one reports a shorter duration than the wall time the load generator actually spent, so tokens/s comes out too high.
problem_statement_precise: `summarize()` in pagedserve/bench/metrics.py computes the run's default duration (when `wall_s` is not passed) as the latest `finish_s` among successful records minus the earliest `arrival_s` over all records. Failed records never contribute, so a failure that gave up after the last success is dropped from the duration and `throughput_tok_s` is inflated (a real run: 46.04 s of duration out of 61.37 s wall, 141 tok/s reported vs ~106 actual). Expected: a failed record should be able to carry the time at which it gave up in a `RequestRecord` field named `end_s` (float seconds on the same clock as `arrival_s`/`finish_s`, default None), and `summarize()` should take the duration as the later of the last successful `finish_s` and the last failed record's `end_s`, minus the first arrival. Concretely, for a successful record arriving at 0.0 and finishing at 10.0 with 100 output tokens plus a failed record (`success=False`, `finish_s=None`) arriving at 1.0 with `end_s=20.0`, the summary should report `duration_s == 20.0`, `throughput_tok_s == 5.0` (only successful tokens count as output) and `completed == 1`.

+    # the run's duration has to include it.

@@ -98,13 +101,18 @@ class BenchSummary:

               slo_tpot_ms: float | None = None, wall_s: float | None = None) -> BenchSummary:
-    """Aggregate. `wall_s` defaults to (last finish - first arrival) over successful
-    records, which is what a load generator measures from first send to last byte."""
+    """Aggregate. `wall_s` defaults to (last end - first arrival): the last successful
+    finish or the last failure, whichever is later, which is what a load generator measures
+    from first send to last byte. (Failures used to be left out, so a run whose failed
+    requests kept timing out after the last success had a shorter duration and a higher
+    throughput than it delivered.) Only successful requests count as output."""
     ok = [r for r in records if r.success and r.finish_s is not None]

-        if ok:

+                                           if not r.success and r.end_s is not None]

+            wall_s = max(ends) - t0

+"""The golden gate's tie-break rule (scripts/check_golden.py): a mismatch is excused only
+when the two disputed tokens are both at the top within the measured noise. It used to
+look at the top-2 gap alone, which also excused an unrelated wrong token whenever the top
+two happened to be close."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import torch
+
+from pagedserve.sched.request import SamplingParams
+from tests.test_engine import make_engine, prompts
+
+sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "scripts"))
+from check_golden import tie_gap  # noqa: E402
+
+
+def test_tie_gap_is_about_the_disputed_pair() -> None:
+    eng = make_engine()
+    ids = prompts(1)[0]
+    req = eng.add_request("probe", ids, SamplingParams.greedy(1))
+    so = eng.scheduler.schedule()
+    with torch.inference_mode():
+        logits = eng.step_logits(so)[0].float()
+    eng.abort_request(req.request_id)
+    eng.backend.free_sequence(req.seq_id)
+    order = torch.argsort(logits, descending=True).tolist()
+    a, b, far = order[0], order[1], order[-1]
+    top2 = float(logits[a] - logits[b])
+    assert abs(tie_gap(eng, ids, a, b) - top2) < 1e-5
+    assert abs(tie_gap(eng, ids, b, a) - top2) < 1e-5
+    # an unrelated token is judged by its own distance from the top, not by the top-2 gap
+    assert tie_gap(eng, ids, far, a) > top2 + 1e-3
+    assert abs(tie_gap(eng, ids, far, a) - float(logits[a] - logits[far])) < 1e-5

meta.commit_subject: Fix the golden gate, the Serverless worker and the benchmark harness (review findings)

problem_statement_vague: In the offline benchmark, requests that queue behind an earlier static batch report latency that leaves out their queue wait, so static batching looks better than it is. Three requests that all arrive at t=0 end up with three different arrival timestamps in the results.
problem_statement_precise: `run_offline_benchmark` in pagedserve/bench/offline.py records each request's arrival (both the `RequestRecord.arrival_s` it returns and the `arrival_time` it passes to `engine.add_request`) as the moment the request was admitted into the engine, not the moment the trace says it was offered (`t0 + req.arrival_s`). With `static_batching=True` and `max_num_seqs=1`, a trace of three requests all with `arrival_s=0.0` is admitted one at a time as each batch drains, so the three records get three distinct `arrival_s` values and their `ttft_s` excludes the time spent waiting for the previous batch. Expected: all three records share one `arrival_s` (the offer time), and their TTFTs strictly increase in admission order because the queued requests waited. The same offset applies to continuous batching, where a request waits for the running step before admission.

meta.commit_subject: Fix the golden gate, the Serverless worker and the benchmark harness (review findings)

problem_statement_vague: Synthetic text prompts produced by the benchmark trace generator repeat: with 100 requests of equal length only about 40 distinct prompts come out, and changing the seed produces the exact same prompts. A server with prefix caching serves the repeats from cache, which distorts the benchmark.
problem_statement_precise: `render_prompt()` in pagedserve/bench/trace.py builds the text body of a synthetic prompt (when `prompt_text` is None and a tokenizer is given) purely from the numeric suffix of `request_id` taken modulo the 40-entry word list `_WORDS`. The body therefore depends only on the request index: for a trace of 100 requests with identical `prompt_len` (and no shared prefix), the rendered prompts collapse to 40 distinct strings, and traces generated with different seeds (e.g. `generate_trace(100, seed=0, ...)` vs `seed=1000`) render identical prompt sets even though their `prompt_ids` differ. Expected: rendered bodies should be as distinct as the trace's seeded `prompt_ids` are, so 100 equal-length requests render 100 distinct prompts, and two seeds render disjoint prompt sets. The shared-prefix words must remain the same leading text for every request, and the padding/truncation to `prompt_len` tokens must still hold. Reproduce with a toy tokenizer whose `encode` splits on whitespace (one id per word) and force every request to the same `prompt_len` with `prompt_ids` of that length.

meta.commit_subject: Fix the golden gate, the Serverless worker and the benchmark harness (review findings)

problem_statement_vague: When benchmarking a chat-completions endpoint, time-to-first-token comes out near zero and the output token count is two too high: the harness is treating the initial role announcement chunk and the final finish chunk as tokens.
problem_statement_precise: The SSE accounting in pagedserve/bench/load.py (`_chunk_text`, used by `_one_request`) treats any chat-completions chunk that has a choice as a token, returning "" when `delta.content` is empty or missing. Two non-token chunks are therefore counted: the opening chunk whose delta only announces the role (`{"delta": {"role": "assistant", "content": ""}, "finish_reason": null}`) becomes the "first token" so `ttft_s` measures the role chunk rather than the first content, and the closing chunk with an empty delta and a `finish_reason` (`{"delta": {}, "finish_reason": "length"}`) counts as an extra output token. For a stream of role chunk, 150 ms pause, two content chunks ("hello", " there"), finish chunk, `[DONE]` against /v1/chat/completions with no `usage`, the record currently has `ttft_s` near 0 and `output_tokens == 4`. Expected: `success=True`, `ttft_s >= 0.14` (measured to the first content chunk), and `output_tokens == 2`. A content chunk whose text is genuinely empty (a partial UTF-8 sequence held back) must still count as a token.

+"""The golden gate's tie-break rule (scripts/check_golden.py): a mismatch is excused only
+when the two disputed tokens are both at the top within the measured noise. It used to
+look at the top-2 gap alone, which also excused an unrelated wrong token whenever the top
+two happened to be close."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import torch
+
+from pagedserve.sched.request import SamplingParams
+from tests.test_engine import make_engine, prompts
+
+sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "scripts"))
+from check_golden import tie_gap  # noqa: E402
+
+
+def test_tie_gap_is_about_the_disputed_pair() -> None:
+    eng = make_engine()
+    ids = prompts(1)[0]
+    req = eng.add_request("probe", ids, SamplingParams.greedy(1))
+    so = eng.scheduler.schedule()
+    with torch.inference_mode():
+        logits = eng.step_logits(so)[0].float()
+    eng.abort_request(req.request_id)
+    eng.backend.free_sequence(req.seq_id)
+    order = torch.argsort(logits, descending=True).tolist()
+    a, b, far = order[0], order[1], order[-1]
+    top2 = float(logits[a] - logits[b])
+    assert abs(tie_gap(eng, ids, a, b) - top2) < 1e-5
+    assert abs(tie_gap(eng, ids, b, a) - top2) < 1e-5
+    # an unrelated token is judged by its own distance from the top, not by the top-2 gap
+    assert tie_gap(eng, ids, far, a) > top2 + 1e-3
+    assert abs(tie_gap(eng, ids, far, a) - float(logits[a] - logits[far])) < 1e-5

meta.commit_subject: Fix the golden gate, the Serverless worker and the benchmark harness (review findings)

problem_statement_vague: The Serverless worker skips downloading the model when a previous cold start was interrupted: a model directory that only has config.json and none of the weight shards is treated as a complete snapshot, and the engine then fails to find weights.
problem_statement_precise: In deploy/runpod/main.py, `resolve_model_dir()` decides that a snapshot is already present (and skips the fetch from `MODEL_REPO`) when `<MODEL_DIR>/config.json` exists. The fetcher writes config.json before any weight shard, so a directory left behind by an interrupted download passes this check with zero shards present. Expected: the worker should expose a predicate `snapshot_complete(model_dir)` in deploy/runpod/main.py (taking a str or PathLike) that returns True only when config.json exists and every weight file is present: if `model.safetensors.index.json` exists, every file named in its `weight_map` values must exist in the directory; otherwise `model.safetensors` must exist. It returns False for a directory with only config.json, for an indexed checkpoint missing any one of its shards, and for a non-existent directory. `resolve_model_dir()` should use this predicate instead of the config.json check.

+    names (or model.safetensors). config.json alone is not enough: the fetcher writes it
+    first, so a directory left by an interrupted download has it and no shards."""

+"""The golden gate's tie-break rule (scripts/check_golden.py): a mismatch is excused only
+when the two disputed tokens are both at the top within the measured noise. It used to
+look at the top-2 gap alone, which also excused an unrelated wrong token whenever the top
+two happened to be close."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import torch
+
+from pagedserve.sched.request import SamplingParams
+from tests.test_engine import make_engine, prompts
+
+sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "scripts"))
+from check_golden import tie_gap  # noqa: E402
+
+
+def test_tie_gap_is_about_the_disputed_pair() -> None:
+    eng = make_engine()
+    ids = prompts(1)[0]
+    req = eng.add_request("probe", ids, SamplingParams.greedy(1))
+    so = eng.scheduler.schedule()
+    with torch.inference_mode():
+        logits = eng.step_logits(so)[0].float()
+    eng.abort_request(req.request_id)
+    eng.backend.free_sequence(req.seq_id)
+    order = torch.argsort(logits, descending=True).tolist()
+    a, b, far = order[0], order[1], order[-1]
+    top2 = float(logits[a] - logits[b])
+    assert abs(tie_gap(eng, ids, a, b) - top2) < 1e-5
+    assert abs(tie_gap(eng, ids, b, a) - top2) < 1e-5
+    # an unrelated token is judged by its own distance from the top, not by the top-2 gap
+    assert tie_gap(eng, ids, far, a) > top2 + 1e-3
+    assert abs(tie_gap(eng, ids, far, a) - float(logits[a] - logits[far])) < 1e-5

meta.commit_subject: Fix the golden gate, the Serverless worker and the benchmark harness (review findings)

problem_statement_vague: Streaming through the Serverless worker is choppy: a token can sit in the output buffer for several hundred milliseconds even though the flush window is 100 ms, because the buffer is only flushed when the next token happens to arrive. The first token of a reply is also held back instead of going out right away.
problem_statement_precise: `_coalesced(chunks, flush_s)` in deploy/runpod/handler.py joins streamed chunks into one output string per `flush_s` window, but it only checks the window when the next chunk arrives from the source iterator. If the source pauses (a slow decode step), whatever is buffered waits for that next chunk: with `flush_s=0.1` and a source yielding "a", then "b" after 20 ms, then "c" after a further 500 ms, "b" is not delivered until "c" arrives (~520 ms), and "a" is likewise buffered rather than delivered immediately. Expected: the stream's first chunk is yielded immediately (well under 50 ms), and a buffered window is yielded when it expires ("b" within 250 ms in that scenario) even if no further chunk has arrived; the output order and content must be preserved ("a", "b", "c" as separate yields in that scenario). Two further properties must hold: an exception raised by the source after "a" was yielded must propagate out of `_coalesced` to the consumer as the same exception (e.g. RuntimeError("upstream broke")) after "a" has already been delivered; and if the consumer stops early (takes one item from a never-ending source then calls `aclose()` on the async generator), `aclose()` must return promptly and leave no background work running. `flush_s <= 0` keeps the pass-through behavior, and empty chunks are still dropped.

+when the two disputed tokens are both at the top within the measured noise. It used to
+look at the top-2 gap alone, which also excused an unrelated wrong token whenever the top
+two happened to be close."""

meta.commit_subject: Fix the golden gate, the Serverless worker and the benchmark harness (review findings)

problem_statement_vague: A Serverless worker configured for tensor parallelism, or for the reference safetensors loader, crashes at cold start when it fetches the model from the Hub: the engine starts reading the model directory while the shards are still downloading and finds nothing there.
problem_statement_precise: In deploy/runpod/main.py, `resolve_model_dir()` streams the download by default: when `MODEL_REPO` is set and no snapshot is present it fetches the small files, kicks off the shards in the background, sets `PAGEDSERVE_WAIT_WEIGHTS_S` in the environment and returns immediately so the engine can start while weights arrive. Only the streaming weight loader on a single rank can wait for shards that are still downloading. With `TENSOR_PARALLEL_SIZE` other than 1, or with `PAGEDSERVE_LOADER=safetensors`, the loader reads whatever files are present and fails on an empty directory. The only way to get a full download today is `WEIGHTS_STREAM=0`. Expected: when `TENSOR_PARALLEL_SIZE` is set to a value other than "1" or `PAGEDSERVE_LOADER` is "safetensors", `resolve_model_dir()` should behave like the `WEIGHTS_STREAM=0` path: call `huggingface_hub.snapshot_download(repo, local_dir=model_dir, revision=..., allow_patterns=...)` exactly once, synchronously, return `model_dir`, and not set `PAGEDSERVE_WAIT_WEIGHTS_S`. After it returns, the directory must count as a complete snapshot under the `snapshot_complete(model_dir)` predicate in the same module (config.json plus `model.safetensors`, or every shard named by `model.safetensors.index.json`). +"""The golden gate's tie-break rule (scripts/check_golden.py): a mismatch is excused only
+when the two disputed tokens are both at the top within the measured noise. It used to
+look at the top-2 gap alone, which also excused an unrelated wrong token whenever the top
+two happened to be close."""
+

+
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import torch
+
+from pagedserve.sched.request import SamplingParams
+from tests.test_engine import make_engine, prompts
+
+sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "scripts"))
+from check_golden import tie_gap  # noqa: E402

+def test_tie_gap_is_about_the_disputed_pair() -> None:
+    eng = make_engine()
+    ids = prompts(1)[0]
+    req = eng.add_request("probe", ids, SamplingParams.greedy(1))
+    so = eng.scheduler.schedule()
+    with torch.inference_mode():
+        logits = eng.step_logits(so)[0].float()
+    eng.abort_request(req.request_id)
+    eng.backend.free_sequence(req.seq_id)
+    order = torch.argsort(logits, descending=True).tolist()
+    a, b, far = order[0], order[1], order[-1]
+    top2 = float(logits[a] - logits[b])
+    assert abs(tie_gap(eng, ids, a, b) - top2) < 1e-5
+    assert abs(tie_gap(eng, ids, b, a) - top2) < 1e-5

+    assert tie_gap(eng, ids, far, a) > top2 + 1e-3

meta.commit_subject: Fix the golden gate, the Serverless worker and the benchmark harness (review findings)

problem_statement_vague: The Serverless worker still streams the weight download, and then crashes at startup, when tensor parallelism is requested through EXTRA_SERVE_ARGS using an abbreviated flag spelling like --tensor-parallel 2, even though the serve CLI accepts that spelling and launches a tensor-parallel server.
problem_statement_precise: `effective_tp_size()` in deploy/runpod/main.py determines whether the launched server will run with tensor parallelism (which decides whether `resolve_model_dir()` must download the whole snapshot before starting rather than streaming it). It reads `TENSOR_PARALLEL_SIZE` and then scans `EXTRA_SERVE_ARGS` for the literal tokens `--tensor-parallel-size <n>` and `--tensor-parallel-size=<n>`. The serve CLI's argparse parser (`pagedserve.cli.build_parser`) also accepts unambiguous prefixes of long options, so `EXTRA_SERVE_ARGS="--tensor-parallel 2"` or `"--tensor-parallel=2"` launches a TP=2 server, yet `effective_tp_size()` returns 1 for them. With `MODEL_REPO` set, an empty `MODEL_DIR`, and `EXTRA_SERVE_ARGS` set to either of those spellings, `resolve_model_dir()` takes the streaming path (sets `PAGEDSERVE_WAIT_WEIGHTS_S`, returns before the shards exist) and the TP loader fails on the empty directory. Expected: for those spellings `effective_tp_size()` returns 2 and `resolve_model_dir()` calls `huggingface_hub.snapshot_download` once, synchronously, leaves `PAGEDSERVE_WAIT_WEIGHTS_S` unset and returns a directory that `snapshot_complete()` accepts, exactly as it already does for `TENSOR_PARALLEL_SIZE=2` and for the full `--tensor-parallel-size` spellings. The worker must agree with whatever the serve command it builds (`serve_command`) will actually parse to, without importing anything heavy.

problem_statement_vague: Step traces are wrong for requests that use a repetition penalty under async scheduling: every step shows zero host resolve time even when resolving the step took tens of milliseconds, and the GPU gap after the engine drains is attributed to host lag.
problem_statement_precise: In `LLMEngine._step_async` (pagedserve/engine.py), when the pending step has any request with `repetition_penalty != 1.0`, the engine takes an early path that resolves the pending step synchronously (`self._resolve(pending, set())`) and finishes its trace record via `tr.finish(pending.trace)` before returning. Unlike the normal resolve path later in the same method, this path never measures the time spent in `_resolve` into the record's `host_resolve_ms` (it stays at its default 0.0 in the written JSONL), and it never calls `tr.idle()` when the resolve leaves the engine with no unfinished requests, so the tracer treats the gap before the next request's first step as host lag. Reproduce with an engine running async scheduling and a `StepTracer` writing to a file (`cuda=False` is fine), one greedy request with `repetition_penalty=1.2` and `max_tokens=4`, `ignore_eos=True`; make `_resolve` take ~20 ms (e.g. a wrapper that sleeps) and step until done. Expected: all four step records in the trace file have `host_resolve_ms` >= 15, and the tracer's `idle()` was called at least once (when the last resolve drained the engine). Currently the records show `host_resolve_ms` of 0 and `idle()` is never called on this path.

index 7e9ca22..79ff443 100644
--- a/pagedserve/engine.py
+++ b/pagedserve/engine.py
@@ -779,9 +786,14 @@ class LLMEngine:
             # token the pending step sampled is not in it yet: launching now would let that
             # token escape the penalty. Resolve first (these steps run synchronously).
             pending, self._pending = self._pending, None
+            t_res = time.perf_counter()
             outputs = self._resolve(pending, set())
-            if pending.trace is not None and tr is not None:
-                tr.finish(pending.trace)
+            if tr is not None:
+                if pending.trace is not None:
+                    pending.trace.host_resolve_ms = (time.perf_counter() - t_res) * 1e3

+                if not self.has_unfinished_requests():
+                    tr.idle()  # drained: the gap before the next request's step is not host lag

problem_statement_vague: Benchmarking pagedserve's own /v1/completions endpoint with a one-token completion gets recorded as a failed "empty stream" request, because the server sends that single token with an empty text and the finish reason in the same chunk and the harness does not count it.
problem_statement_precise: `_chunk_text()` in pagedserve/bench/load.py decides whether an SSE chunk carries a token. For a completions-style choice (one with a `text` key), it now returns None when `finish_reason` is non-null and the text is empty, treating the chunk as a pure closing chunk. But pagedserve sends its last token in the same chunk as the finish reason, and that token's text can legitimately be empty (the detokenizer suppressed it), so a one-token completion streamed as `{"choices": [{"text": "", "finish_reason": "length"}], "usage": {"prompt_tokens": 3, "completion_tokens": 1}}` followed by `[DONE]` is recorded as `success=False` with error "empty stream". Expected: a completions choice is always a token, even with empty text and a finish reason, so that request is `success=True` with `output_tokens == 1` and `ttft_s` measured at that chunk's arrival (>= 0.015 when the chunk is delayed 20 ms). The chat-completions rules must stay as they are: a usage-only trailer with no choices, a role-only chunk (`delta` with `role` and empty content) and a closing chat chunk whose `delta` has no content are not tokens.

index 69d866c..bbfc4d2 100644
--- a/pagedserve/bench/load.py
+++ b/pagedserve/bench/load.py
@@ -39,24 +39,23 @@ def _parse_sse_line(line: str) -> dict | None:

-    """Text delta from a completions or chat-completions stream chunk; None if the chunk
-    carries no token: a usage-only trailer, a chat chunk that only announces the role, or a
-    closing chunk with an empty delta and a finish reason. (Counting those made the role
-    chunk the "first token" and the closing chunk an extra one.) A token whose text is
-    empty (a partial UTF-8 sequence held back) still counts, as ""."""
+    """Text delta of a completions or chat-completions stream chunk that carries a token;
+    None for a chunk that carries none: a usage-only trailer (no choices), a chat chunk that
+    only announces the role, or a chat closing chunk whose delta has no content. (The role
+    chunk used to count as the first token.) A completions choice is always a token, and
+    its text may be empty (a partial UTF-8 sequence held back, or a final token the
+    detokenizer suppressed, which pagedserve sends together with the finish reason)."""
     choices = obj.get("choices") or []
     if not choices:
         return None
     c = choices[0]
-    finishing = c.get("finish_reason") is not None

-        text = c["text"] or ""
-        return None if (finishing and not text) else text
+        return c["text"] or ""

     content = delta.get("content")
-    if not content and (finishing or "role" in delta or content is None):
+    if content is None or (content == "" and "role" in delta):

-    return content or ""
+    return content

problem_statement_vague: Benchmarks against vLLM report an inflated time-per-output-token: vLLM's completions stream ends with a separate usage-only chunk that arrives well after the last token, and the harness treats that trailer as if it were the last token.
problem_statement_precise: In `_one_request` in pagedserve/bench/load.py, a chunk that carries no token (`_chunk_text` returns None) is skipped, except that once the stream is known to be complete (a choice with a non-null `finish_reason` was seen) and a first token exists, the skipped chunk's arrival time is assigned to `last`, the "last token" time used by `RequestRecord.tpot_s` and `finish_s`. vLLM's /v1/completions stream sends a usage-only trailer (`{"choices": [], "usage": {...}}`) after the final token, so that trailer moves `last`: two tokens 11 ms apart followed by a trailer 150 ms later yields a TPOT of ~160 ms instead of ~11 ms. Expected: `last` only advances on chunks that carry a token; trailers and closing chunks that carry no token leave it unchanged, while their `usage` is still read for the token counts. For the stream above (`{"text": "a", "finish_reason": null}`, 11 ms later `{"text": "b", "finish_reason": "length"}`, 150 ms later the usage trailer with `completion_tokens: 2`, then `[DONE]`) against /v1/completions, the record must be `success=True`, `output_tokens == 2`, and `tpot_s < 0.05`.
patch:
diff --git a/pagedserve/bench/load.py b/pagedserve/bench/load.py
index 69d866c..bbfc4d2 100644
--- a/pagedserve/bench/load.py
+++ b/pagedserve/bench/load.py
@@ -113,9 +112,7 @@ async def _one_request(client: httpx.AsyncClient, model: str, req: TraceRequest,
                     if _chunk_finished(obj):
                         completed = True
                     if _chunk_text(obj) is None:
-                        if completed and first is not None:
-                            last = now  # the closing chunk ends the request
-                        continue
+                        continue  # `last` stays the last token's time (TPOT), not a trailer's
                     n_chunks += 1
                     if first is None:
                         first = now

problem_statement_vague: When the engine core subprocess fails to start (for example the model path does not exist), the API side raises as expected but leaves a stray writer thread and open pipe file descriptors behind, and calling send() on the dead handle fails with an assertion instead of a clear error.
problem_statement_precise: `EngineCoreProcess.start()` in pagedserve/server/engine_core.py creates the `_CommandWriter` (a daemon thread named "pagedserve-core-writer") right after spawning the core, before the core has reported ready. If the core then sends a "fatal" message or exits during startup, `start()` raises RuntimeError ("engine core failed to start: ..." or "engine core process exited during startup") without cleaning up: the writer thread keeps running, `_writer`, `_cmd_send` and `_out_recv` stay set, and the pipes remain open (only the timeout path calls `stop()`). Afterwards `send()` fails with an AssertionError if `_writer` is None, which is not a meaningful error. Reproduce by constructing `EngineCoreProcess(EngineSpec(EngineConfig(device="cpu"), model_dir=<non-existent path>))` and calling `start()`. Expected: `start()` still raises RuntimeError matching "failed to start" or "exited during startup", but after the exception `core.alive` is False, `core._writer is None`, `core._cmd_send is None`, no thread named "pagedserve-core-writer" is alive, and `core.send(("abort", "x"))` raises RuntimeError with a message containing "not running". The same cleanup should apply on the timeout path.
patch:
diff --git a/pagedserve/server/engine_core.py b/pagedserve/server/engine_core.py
index d91a30b..16aeddf 100644
--- a/pagedserve/server/engine_core.py
+++ b/pagedserve/server/engine_core.py
@@ -370,24 +370,30 @@ class EngineCoreProcess:
     def start(self, ready_timeout_s: float = 900.0) -> dict[str, Any]:
         self._proc, [(cmd_send, out_recv)] = spawn_core(self.spec, 1)
         self._cmd_send, self._out_recv = cmd_send, out_recv
-        self._writer = _CommandWriter(cmd_send)
         deadline = time.monotonic() + ready_timeout_s
-        while True:
-            if out_recv.poll(1.0):
-                msg = out_recv.recv()
-                if msg[0] == "ready":
-                    self.info = msg[1]
-                    return self.info
-                if msg[0] == "fatal":
-                    raise RuntimeError(f"engine core failed to start:\n{msg[1]}")
-            if not self._proc.is_alive():
-                raise RuntimeError("engine core process exited during startup")
-            if time.monotonic() > deadline:
-                self.stop()
-                raise TimeoutError("engine core did not become ready")
+        try:
+            while True:
+                if out_recv.poll(1.0):
+                    msg = out_recv.recv()
+                    if msg[0] == "ready":
+                        self.info = msg[1]
+                        # Nothing is sent before the core is ready; starting the writer only
+                        # now means a failed start leaves no thread behind.
+                        self._writer = _CommandWriter(cmd_send)
+                        return self.info
+                    if msg[0] == "fatal":
+                        raise RuntimeError(f"engine core failed to start:\n{msg[1]}")
+                if not self._proc.is_alive():
+                    raise RuntimeError("engine core process exited during startup")
+                if time.monotonic() > deadline:
+                    raise TimeoutError("engine core did not become ready")
+        except BaseException:
+            self.stop(timeout_s=5.0)  # the process, its pipes
+            raise
 
     def send(self, msg: tuple) -> None:
-        assert self._writer is not None
+        if self._writer is None:
+            raise RuntimeError("engine core is not running")
         self._writer.put(msg)
 
     def recv(self, timeout: float | None = None) -> tuple | None:

meta.commit_subject: Fix what the follow-up review found in the first round of fixes

problem_statement_vague: On a Runpod cold start with the model fetched from the Hub, passing tensor parallelism through the extra serve-args env var instead of the dedicated TP env var makes the engine start on an empty model directory and fail, because the worker still starts streaming the shards in the background as if it were a single rank.
problem_statement_precise: In deploy/runpod/main.py, resolve_model_dir() decides whether the weights can be streamed into the engine while shards are still downloading (one rank, streaming loader) or must be fully downloaded with snapshot_download first (tensor parallelism, or PAGEDSERVE_LOADER=safetensors). The decision only looks at the TENSOR_PARALLEL_SIZE environment variable. But serve_command() appends EXTRA_SERVE_ARGS last, so `EXTRA_SERVE_ARGS="--tensor-parallel-size 2"` or `EXTRA_SERVE_ARGS="--tensor-parallel-size=2"` (with TENSOR_PARALLEL_SIZE unset) actually launches a TP=2 server. In that configuration resolve_model_dir() still takes the streaming path: it starts the background Fetcher, sets PAGEDSERVE_WAIT_WEIGHTS_S, and returns immediately, and the TP engine then reads an incomplete directory and fails. problem_statement_vague: Serving a 7B fp16 model on a 24 GB card, the engine allocates only the minimum KV cache (a few dozen blocks), so only about 30 sequences fit and throughput is a third of what the card should do. On an 80 GB card the cache is also noticeably smaller than expected, but it is not obvious there.
problem_statement_precise: pagedserve/engine.py default_num_blocks() computes the CUDA KV-cache budget as `free * gpu_memory_utilization - model_bytes - 512 MiB`, floored at 64 blocks. But `free` comes from torch.cuda.mem_get_info() after the weights are already loaded, so the weights are subtracted twice. For Qwen2-7B (hidden 3584, 28 layers, 28 heads, 4 KV heads; 14.7 MB per 256-token fp16 block) on an RTX 4090 with ~15.2 GB of weights resident and ~9.5 GB free, the budget goes negative and the engine lands on the 64-block floor (16K tokens of cache) when roughly 570 blocks fit. Expected: the budget is `int(free * utilization) - workspace` with no weight subtraction, floored at the minimum block count; with 9500 MiB free and utilization 0.90 that yields `(int(free*0.90) - 512 MiB) // bytes_per_block` (>= 500 blocks), and a free value of 0 yields the 64-block floor. The hidden test imports the pure budget function from pagedserve.engine as `kv_blocks_for(free_bytes, utilization, bytes_per_block)` together with module constants `KV_WORKSPACE_BYTES` (512 MiB) and `MIN_GPU_BLOCKS` (64), so the budget arithmetic must be factored out under those names and default_num_blocks should use it (it no longer needs the model's byte count).

+KV_WORKSPACE_BYTES = 512 << 20  # activations, graph pools, sampler scratch outside the cache
+MIN_GPU_BLOCKS = 64

+def kv_blocks_for(free_bytes: int, utilization: float, bytes_per_block: int) -> int:
+    """KV blocks that fit in `free_bytes` of device memory read *with the weights already
+    resident*: `free * utilization - workspace`, floored at MIN_GPU_BLOCKS.
+
+    The weights are not subtracted here. They used to be, on top of a `free` that already
+    excluded them, and an 80 GB card never noticed (7B: 42 GB of cache instead of 57) while
+    a 24 GB card serving the 7B went to the 64-block floor — 16K tokens of cache, about 30
+    sequences in flight, 1,118 tok/s on an RTX 4090 where the batch should have been KV-bound
+    at three times that."""
+    budget = int(free_bytes * utilization) - KV_WORKSPACE_BYTES
+    return max(budget // bytes_per_block, MIN_GPU_BLOCKS)

+    blocks (block_size 16 -> 32K cached tokens), which is ~800 MB at fp32 for the 0.5B
+    model and plenty for local correctness work.

problem_statement_vague: With async scheduling turned on, a request using a repetition penalty produces different tokens than the same request with async scheduling off; it starts repeating a token that the penalty should have suppressed. Requests without a penalty are unaffected.
problem_statement_precise: LLMEngine.step() in pagedserve/engine.py, with EngineConfig(async_scheduling=True), launches the next step before the previous step's sampled token has been read back from the device and appended to each request's token history (all_token_ids). The repetition penalty in the sampler is computed on the host from that history, so the token sampled by the still-pending step is not penalized in the next step and can be sampled again. meta.commit_subject: Fix engine defects found in an external review

problem_statement_vague: The engine's memory grows without bound in a long-running server: the final text of every finished request is kept around forever, and even resetting the engine between benchmark runs does not release it.
problem_statement_precise: LLMEngine in pagedserve/engine.py stores the detokenized final text of each finished request in `self._final_text` (filled in when a request finishes, in the step's output handling) so that `output_text(request_id)` can return it later. Nothing in the HTTP server path or LLM.generate ever calls output_text, so entries are never popped and the dict grows by one entry per request for the life of the process; `reset()` also leaves it intact. Expected: the retained finished-text map is bounded to a fixed number of most-recently-finished requests, evicting the oldest first (insertion order), and `reset()` clears it entirely. The hidden test monkeypatches a module-level constant `FINAL_TEXT_KEEP` in pagedserve.engine to 5, runs 12 requests r0..r11 (greedy 2 tokens each) through the default test engine until none remain, and expects `list(eng._final_text) == ['r7', ..., 'r11']`, then `eng.reset()` and `not eng._final_text`. So the cap must be a module constant with that name read at eviction time, and `_final_text` must iterate in insertion order.

meta.commit_subject: Fix engine defects found in an external review

problem_statement_vague: Under load with streaming clients, the API server can freeze completely: no responses come out and new requests hang, while the engine-core subprocess is still alive. It happens when a client stops reading and the engine's output pipe fills up.
problem_statement_precise: EngineCoreProcess.send() in pagedserve/server/engine_core.py writes commands directly into the command pipe on the caller's thread under a lock. The core process only reads commands between steps, so when it blocks writing a step's outputs into a full output pipe, the output reader thread on the API side (the only thing draining that pipe) blocks the moment it tries to send a stop-string abort, and the event loop blocks holding the send lock midway through a large `add`; nothing drains anything and the server deadlocks. Expected: sending a command to the core must never block the caller, even when nobody is reading the pipe and the payload is far larger than the pipe buffer (e.g. a 4 MiB add followed by two aborts returns in well under 0.5 s), and the messages must arrive in the order they were submitted. When the receiving end of the pipe has been closed, the first write fails asynchronously; the failure must be exposed on the writer as an `error` attribute (the caught exception, None until then), and any subsequent submission must raise BrokenPipeError. The hidden test exercises this through a helper class `_CommandWriter(conn)` in pagedserve.server.engine_core that takes a multiprocessing Connection, with `put(msg)`, an `error` attribute and `close()`; EngineCoreProcess.send should go through it.
patch:
diff --git a/pagedserve/server/engine_core.py b/pagedserve/server/engine_core.py
index 6c57429..d91a30b 100644
--- a/pagedserve/server/engine_core.py
+++ b/pagedserve/server/engine_core.py
@@ -20,7 +20,9 @@ from __future__ import annotations
 
 import multiprocessing as mp
 import os
+import queue
 import sys
+import threading
 import time
 import traceback
 from dataclasses import dataclass, field
@@ -305,8 +307,52 @@ def spawn_core(spec: EngineSpec, n_workers: int = 1) -> tuple[Any, list[tuple[Co
     return proc, chans
 
 
+_CLOSE = object()
+
+
+class _CommandWriter:
+    """Writes commands into the core's pipe on a thread of its own, so `send` never blocks.
+
+    With a blocking `send`, the API side could deadlock against the core: the core blocks
+    writing a step's outputs into a full output pipe (its loop reads commands only between
+    steps), the output reader thread, which is the only thing draining that pipe, blocks
+    sending a stop-string abort, and the event loop holds the send lock mid-way through a
+    large `add` that the core will never read. Queuing the writes keeps the reader draining
+    and the event loop running whatever the pipes' state; one thread keeps the order."""
+
+    def __init__(self, conn: Connection) -> None:
+        self._conn = conn
+        self._q: queue.SimpleQueue = queue.SimpleQueue()
+        self.error: BaseException | None = None
+        self._thread = threading.Thread(target=self._run, name="pagedserve-core-writer",
+                                        daemon=True)
+        self._thread.start()
+
+    def put(self, msg: tuple) -> None:
+        if self.error is not None:
+            raise BrokenPipeError(f"engine core pipe closed: {self.error!r}")
+        self._q.put(msg)
+
+    def _run(self) -> None:
+        while True:
+            msg = self._q.get()
+            if msg is _CLOSE:
+                return
+            try:
+                self._conn.send(msg)
+            except (OSError, EOFError, ValueError) as exc:  # the core is gone
+                self.error = exc
+                return
+
+    def close(self, timeout_s: float = 5.0) -> None:
+        """Let the queued commands go out (up to `timeout_s`), then stop the thread."""
+        self._q.put(_CLOSE)
+        self._thread.join(timeout_s)
+

meta.commit_subject: Fix engine defects found in an external review

problem_statement_vague: The Triton paged-attention decode kernel breaks for KV block sizes that are multiples of 16 but not powers of two: block size 48 errors out in the dot variant, and block size 96 reads the wrong keys for positions past 64, so attention output is wrong once a context grows beyond that.
problem_statement_precise: paged_attention_decode() in pagedserve/attn/paged_triton.py picks a per-block tile (positions processed per kernel iteration). For the dot variant the tile is `min(block_size, 64)`, and _tile_for() rounds a tile down to a power of two then takes `min(block_size, tile)`. The engine accepts any block_size that is a multiple of 16, so with block_size=48 the dot variant gets a 48-position tile, which is not a power of two and `tl.arange` rejects it (the kernel fails to compile/launch); with block_size=96 it gets a 64-position tile that does not divide the page, so positions 64..95 of each block are read from the next physical block and the result is wrong. Expected: for block sizes 48 and 96, in both the `sum` and `dot` variants, with 6 physical blocks, block tables like [4, 1] and [0, 5, 2] and context lengths block_size+20 and 2*block_size+5 (crossing both the 64 mark and page boundaries), num_splits=1 and scale D**-0.5, the output must match a causal softmax attention reference over the gathered K/V within the usual test tolerance. The tile chosen must always be a power of two that divides block_size (16 always qualifies).

     tile = max(16, min(32, TILE_BUDGET // (groups_pad * head_dim)))
-    tile = 1 << (tile.bit_length() - 1)  # round down to a power of two
-    return min(block_size, tile)
+    return _pow2_divisor(block_size, tile)
+

+    """The largest power of two <= `cap` that divides `block_size` (16 always does). A tile

+    tile was 48, not a power of two, which `tl.arange` rejects."""
+    t = 1 << (max(cap, 1).bit_length() - 1)
+    while t > 1 and block_size % t:
+        t //= 2
+    return t

problem_statement_vague: Without chunked prefill, a request that gets preempted after generating a while can get stuck forever in the waiting queue even though every KV block is free, and everything queued behind it never runs.
problem_statement_precise: Scheduler._schedule_prefill() in pagedserve/sched/scheduler.py admits waiting requests only while `budget + query_len <= max_num_batched_tokens`. A request admitted with a 4-token prompt under max_num_batched_tokens=8 can grow past 8 tokens before being preempted; when it comes back to the head of `waiting`, its query_len alone exceeds the budget, the loop breaks every step, and it waits forever (a reviewer saw a 13-token request waiting with every block free), blocking the queue behind it. meta.commit_subject: Fix engine defects found in an external review

problem_statement_vague: Loading an untied checkpoint under tensor parallelism fails with a shape mismatch on the output head when the vocabulary size is not divisible by the number of ranks.
problem_statement_precise: When the vocabulary cannot be split evenly across ranks (e.g. vocab_size 257 over tp_size 2), Qwen2ForCausalLM in pagedserve/model/qwen2.py keeps the whole lm_head on every rank and sets `lm_head_sharded = False`. But _load_tensors() in pagedserve/model/weights.py (reached via load_hf_state_dict with a TPState) unconditionally runs the checkpoint tensor through tpdist.shard_tensor for every parameter, so an untied checkpoint's `lm_head.weight` is sliced to (129, 64) and the shape check against the model's (257, 64) parameter raises ValueError('shape mismatch ...'). Repro: ModelConfig.tiny(vocab_size=257, tie_word_embeddings=False); build the full model with tp_size=1, reset parameters deterministically, take hf_state_dict(); then for rank 0 and 1 build Qwen2ForCausalLM(cfg.shard(2), tp_size=2) (lm_head_sharded is False) and call load_hf_state_dict(shard, sd, tp=TPState(rank, 2)). Expected: loading succeeds and each rank's `lm_head.weight` is exactly equal to the full model's `lm_head.weight`. Sharding of every other parameter (and of lm_head when it is sharded) must be unchanged.

meta.commit_subject: Runpod worker: coalesce streamed yields per STREAM_FLUSH_MS (each yield is a platform round trip: one stream ran at 9 tok/s with the engine idle); RUNPOD_LB=1 load-balancing mode runs pagedserve serve on $PORT directly; /ping route; docs

problem_statement_vague: Streaming completions through the Runpod queue worker are very slow, around 9 tokens per second, even though the engine itself is nearly idle; every token becomes its own round trip to the platform.
problem_statement_precise:
The Runpod job handler in deploy/runpod/handler.py (make_handler) relays the server's SSE stream to the platform by yielding each chunk as it arrives. On Runpod every yield is a platform round trip, so a single stream is bottlenecked at ~9 tok/s regardless of engine speed. Expected: chunks are batched by time before yielding. Provide an async generator in handler.py, `_coalesced(chunks, flush_s)`, that takes an async iterator of strings and a window in seconds and yields the concatenation of the chunks received within each window; the first chunk of a window starts that window's clock (so an idle stream still delivers its first token immediately), and whatever is buffered when the source ends is flushed. The concatenation of all yielded strings must equal the concatenation of all input chunks, in order. With six chunks `data: 0

` ... `data: 5

` arriving 30 ms apart and flush_s=0.1, the output must have more than 1 and fewer than 6 items; with flush_s=0 (or negative) every non-empty chunk is yielded individually, unchanged. The handler should use this with a STREAM_FLUSH_MS environment variable (default 100) controlling the window.
patch:
diff --git a/deploy/runpod/handler.py b/deploy/runpod/handler.py
index 548b905..8bd3544 100644
--- a/deploy/runpod/handler.py
+++ b/deploy/runpod/handler.py
@@ -23,6 +23,7 @@ relays them to the caller); otherwise the parsed JSON response is yielded once.
 from __future__ import annotations
 
 import os
+import time
 from typing import Any, AsyncIterator
 
 import httpx
@@ -56,6 +62,29 @@ def _error(message: str, error_type: str = "worker_error") -> dict[str, Any]:
     return {"error": {"message": message, "type": error_type, "code": None}}
 
 
+async def _coalesced(chunks: AsyncIterator[str], flush_s: float) -> AsyncIterator[str]:
+    """Join `chunks` into one string per `flush_s` window (the first chunk of a window
+    starts its clock, so an idle stream still delivers its first token at once)."""
+    if flush_s <= 0:
+        async for chunk in chunks:
+            if chunk:
+                yield chunk
+        return
+    buf: list[str] = []
+    started = 0.0
+    async for chunk in chunks:
+        if not chunk:
+            continue
+        if not buf:
+            started = time.monotonic()
+        buf.append(chunk)
+        if time.monotonic() - started >= flush_s:
+            yield "".join(buf)
+            buf = []
+    if buf:
+        yield "".join(buf)
+
+

When the Runpod worker streams weights at start, the shards are still downloading when the CLI runs, so a 16 GB Qwen3-8B sums to a few bytes and is treated as small. Expected: when `model.safetensors.index.json` exists in the directory and its `metadata.total_size` is present and non-zero, checkpoint_bytes returns that value as an int (e.g. 16_381_470_720 for an index with that total_size even though no shard file is present, which is > SMALL_CHECKPOINT_BYTES); when the index has no metadata/total_size, fall back to summing the `*.safetensors` files present (an index with only `weight_map: {}` plus a 10-byte model.safetensors returns 10). problem_statement_vague: When a log containing a PEM private key is landed, only the first line of the key is masked; the base64 body of the key is copied into the landing directory in the clear.
problem_statement_precise: In lakehouse/redact.py the `private_key` pattern matches only the `-----BEGIN ... PRIVATE KEY-----` header line, so `redact()` replaces the header with `<redacted:private_key>` and leaves the key material and footer in the output, and `find()` on the redacted output is still empty, so nothing downstream notices. Expected: the entire PEM block — header, body, and `-----END ... PRIVATE KEY-----` footer — is replaced by a single `<redacted:private_key>`, counted once under `private_key`, with the text before and after the block preserved (for `before\n<pem>\nafter` the output starts with `before` and ends with `after`, and contains none of the body lines). A truncated block that has a header but no footer must be redacted from the header to the end of the text and counted once under the separate name `private_key_truncated` (same `<redacted:private_key>` replacement text). Reproduce: build a block from `-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----`, five lines starting `MIIE`, and the matching END line; `redact()` currently leaves `MIIE` in the output.

     ("aws_access_key", re.compile(r"(?:AKIA|ASIA)[0-9A-Z]{16}"),                "<redacted:aws_access_key>"),
     ("slack_token",   re.compile(r"xox[abprs]-[A-Za-z0-9-]{10,}"),             "<redacted:slack_token>"),
-    ("private_key",   re.compile(r"-----BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY-----"),        "<redacted:private_key>"),
+    # whole PEM block, header to footer; a truncated block (no footer) is redacted to the end of the text
+    ("private_key",   re.compile(r"-----BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY-----[\s\S]*?-----END [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY-----"), "<redacted:private_key>"),
+    ("private_key_truncated", re.compile(r"-----BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY-----[\s\S]*"), "<redacted:private_key>"),

problem_statement_vague: An external audit pushed a batch of credential shapes through the landing step and they came out unchanged: HTTP Basic auth headers, passwords embedded in database URLs, API keys in query strings, Google/Stripe/SendGrid keys and Slack webhook URLs, plus short passwords and passwords containing punctuation after `PASSWORD=`. Meanwhile placeholder values like `hf_REDACTED` and `xxxxxxxxxxxx` are at risk of being flagged.
problem_statement_precise: `redact()`/`find()` in lakehouse/redact.py (one PATTERNS list of `(name, regex, replacement)`, replacement `<redacted:NAME>`) miss several shapes. Expected, each as its own named pattern producing `<redacted:name>` and one hit under that name: `basic_auth` — `Authorization: Basic QWxhZGRpbjpvcGVuIHNlc2FtZQ==` (replacement keeps the `Basic ` prefix); `url_password` — the password in `postgres://admin:S3cretPass@host/db` (user name kept, `@` kept); `query_secret` — `?key=abcdefgh1234&x=1` style `?`/`&` parameters named key/api_key/token/access_token/secret/password with 8+ char values; `google_api_key` — `AIza` + 35 chars; `stripe_key` — `sk_live_`/`sk_test_`/`rk_` + 16+ alphanumerics; `sendgrid_key` — `SG.<22+>.<43+>`; `slack_webhook` — `https://hooks.slack.com/services/T.../B.../<16+>`. The existing `kv_secret` pattern requires a 16+ character value of `[A-Za-z0-9+/=._-]`, so it misses `password = hunter2xx` (short value), `DB_PASSWORD="Tr0ub4dor&3!xyz"` (punctuation), and for `SECRET=aaaaaaaa!bbbbbbbb` would stop at the `!`; expected: values of 8+ characters running to the next whitespace, quote, comma, semicolon, closing bracket or `<`, replaced whole, so `redact("SECRET=aaaaaaaa!bbbbbbbb")[0] == "SECRET=<redacted:kv_secret>"`. Purely numeric values of any length remain non-secrets, and `find()` must return `[]` for the placeholders `'hf_token': 'hf_REDACTED'`, `YOUR_API_KEY=your_api_key_here`, `API_KEY=xxxxxxxxxxxx`, `api_key: changeme-now`, and for `"workers_before": "{\"idle\": 1}"`. Existing tests on hf/runpod/sk/github/aws/slack/jwt/bearer/private-key shapes must keep passing.

     ("private_key_truncated", re.compile(r"-----BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY-----[\s\S]*"), "<redacted:private_key>"),
     ("jwt",           re.compile(r"eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]{10,}\.eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]{10,}\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{10,}"), "<redacted:jwt>"),
+    ("google_api_key", re.compile(r"AIza[0-9A-Za-z_\-]{35}"),                   "<redacted:google_api_key>"),
+    ("stripe_key",    re.compile(r"[sr]k_(?:live|test)_[A-Za-z0-9]{16,}"),      "<redacted:stripe_key>"),
+    ("sendgrid_key",  re.compile(r"SG\.[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{16,}\.[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{16,}"), "<redacted:sendgrid_key>"),
+    ("slack_webhook", re.compile(r"https://hooks\.slack\.com/services/T[A-Za-z0-9]+/B[A-Za-z0-9]+/[A-Za-z0-9]{16,}"),
+     "<redacted:slack_webhook>"),
     ("bearer",        re.compile(r"(?i)\bbearer\s+[A-Za-z0-9._+/=\-]{20,}"),    "Bearer <redacted:bearer>"),
+    ("basic_auth",    re.compile(r"(?i)\bbasic\s+[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{16,}"),         "Basic <redacted:basic_auth>"),

diff --git a/tests/test_gold_boot_phases.py b/tests/test_gold_boot_phases.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..4dfe786
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/test_gold_boot_phases.py
@@ -0,0 +1,90 @@
+"""Boot segmentation in gold_worker_boot_phases, on a synthetic silver_worker_log_events frame.
+
+The fourth audit found the previous rule ("a boot opens at `Starting vLLM:`") merged two boots that shared one
+wrapper line into a chimera row and dropped boots with no wrapper line at all. Starts a JVM, so marked slow.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import shutil
+from datetime import datetime, timezone
+
+import pytest
+
+pytestmark = [pytest.mark.slow, pytest.mark.skipif(shutil.which("java") is None, reason="needs a JVM")]
+
+
+def ts(minute: int, second: int = 0):
+    return datetime(2026, 9, 23, 18, minute, second, tzinfo=timezone.utc).replace(tzinfo=None)
+
+
+def ev(spark, rows):
+    """rows: (source_file, worker_id, line_no, minute, second, message)."""
+    from pyspark.sql import types as T
+    schema = T.StructType([T.StructField("source_file", T.StringType()), T.StructField("worker_id", T.StringType()),
+                           T.StructField("line_no", T.IntegerType()), T.StructField("ts_utc", T.TimestampType()),
+                           T.StructField("ts_format", T.StringType()), T.StructField("event_kind", T.StringType()),
+                           T.StructField("message", T.StringType())])
+    return spark.createDataFrame([(f, w, n, ts(m, s), "pipe", "vllm", msg) for f, w, n, m, s, msg in rows], schema)
+
+
+BOOT_LINES = [  # one complete boot, offsets in seconds from its first line
+    (0, "Starting vLLM: vllm serve --host 127.0.0.1"),
+    (45, "Initializing a V1 LLM engine (v0.28.0) with config: model='qwen/qwen3-8b'"),
+    (90, "Loading weights took 18.12 seconds"),
+    (150, "Graph capturing finished in 6 secs, took 0.58 GiB"),
+    (160, "Graph capturing finished in 7 secs, took 0.58 GiB"),
+    (165, "init engine (profile, create kv cache, warmup model) took 56.34 s (compilation: 37.27 s)"),
+    (170, "Application startup complete."),
+]
+
+
+def boot(file, worker, line0, minute0, lines=BOOT_LINES, skip_start=False):
+    out = []
+    for i, (off, msg) in enumerate(lines):
+        if skip_start and msg.startswith("Starting vLLM:"):
+            continue
+        out.append((file, worker, line0 + i, minute0 + off // 60, off % 60, msg))
+    return out
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
+def spark():
+    from lakehouse.spark import get_spark
+    s = get_spark("parquet", app="test-boot-phases")
+    yield s
+    s.stop()
+
+
+def test_segmentation_opens_boots_at_wrapper_or_orphan_init_and_keeps_headless_boots(spark):
+    from lakehouse.gold import worker_boot_phases
+    rows = (
+        boot("a.log", "w1", 1, 0)                                   # ordinary boot: wrapper + init
+        + boot("a.log", "w1", 100, 10, skip_start=True)             # same worker, console missed the wrapper line → orphan init
+        + boot("a.log", "w2", 200, 20, skip_start=True)             # another worker interleaved, no wrapper line at all
+        + boot("b.log", None, 1, 30, lines=BOOT_LINES[2:])          # log starts mid-boot: no wrapper, no init
+        + boot("c.log", None, 1, 40) + boot("c.log", None, 50, 50)  # two clean restarts in one log
+    )
+    out = {(r.source_file, r.worker_id or "", r.boot_index): r for r in worker_boot_phases(ev(spark, rows)).collect()}
+    assert len(out) == 6, sorted(out)
+
